'''Vitaly Kocharovsky''' is a Russian-American [[physicist]], academic and researcher. He is a Professor of Physics and Astronomy at [[Texas A&M University]].<ref name=OOP>{{cite web|url=https://physics.tamu.edu/directory/vitaly-kocharovsky/|title=Vitaly Kocharovsky|date=30 September 2019 }}</ref>

Kocharovsky has focused his research on topics in theoretical physics, including [[quantum gravity]], [[critical phenomena]], [[superradiance]], [[quantum optics]], [[laser physics]], semiconductor [[optoelectronics]], wave propagation and mode coupling in inhomogeneous media, magnetospheric physics, plasma astrophysics, gamma- and radio-astronomy, and high-energy cosmic rays.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ras.ru/publishing/nature.aspx|title=Ежемесячный естественнонаучный журнал РАН}}</ref>

==Education==
Kocharovsky received his Master's degree in Physics and Mathematics from [[N. I. Lobachevsky State University of Nizhny Novgorod|N.I. Lobachevsky State University of Nizhny Novgorod]], Russia in 1978 and Doctoral Degree in Physics and Mathematics from [[Radiophysical Research Institute]] in 1986. He was awarded Dr. of Sciences (Habilitation) Degree in Physics and Mathematics by the Highest Attestation Commission of the Russian Federation in 1998 after completing the habilitation thesis titled "Collective effects of [[spontaneous emission]] and quantum theory of dissipative instability".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://search.rsl.ru/ru/record/01000043545|title=Collective effects of spontaneous emission and the quantum theory of dissipative instability: abstract of thesis. ... doctors of physical and mathematical sciences}}</ref>

==Career==
Kocharovsky started his career as a Researcher at the Institute of Applied Physics of the Russian Academy of Sciences<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ipfran.ru/institute/info|title=General Information}}</ref> in 1978, and became a Senior Researcher in 1986, and a Leading Researcher in 1996. He held his next appointment at Texas A&M University as an Associate Research Scientist in the Department of Physics in 1998, served as Visiting Associate Professor in 2001, and was promoted to Associate Professor of Physics in 2002, and to Professor of Physics and Astronomy in 2005.<ref name=OOP/>

Kocharovsky found a negative-energy mechanism of instability in the [[quantum field theory]] of a gravity-matter system and discussed its manifestation in a cosmological model.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Nonlinear dynamics of gravity and matter creation in a cosmology with an unbounded Hamiltonian|year=2004 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.70.066210 |last1=Akguc |first1=Gursoy B. |last2=Reichl |first2=L. E. |last3=Derishev |first3=E. V. |last4=Kocharovsky |first4=Vl. V. |last5=Kocharovsky |first5=V. V. |journal=Physical Review E |volume=70 |issue=6 |article-number=066210 |pmid=15697487 |bibcode=2004PhRvE..70f6210A }}</ref> He stated that a similar mechanism of a dissipative instability is responsible for a superradiance<ref>{{cite web|url=http://83.149.229.155/cgi-bin/e/index/e/60/5/p897?a=list|title=Superradiance and dissipative instability in an inverted two-level system}}</ref> and predicted new regimes of superradiant lasing and nonequilibrium phase transitions in an atom-light system. In 1997, he predicted a phenomenon of a collective electron-positron annihilation and an electron-hole recombination.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Collective QED processes of electron - hole recombination and electron - positron annihilation in a strong magnetic field|year=1997 |doi=10.1088/1355-5111/9/1/002 |last1=Belyanin |first1=A. A. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=V. V. |last3=Kocharovsky |first3=Vl V. |journal=Quantum and Semiclassical Optics: Journal of the European Optical Society Part B |volume=9 |pages=1–44 }}</ref> The latter phenomenon has been later observed experimentally.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Cooperative Recombination of a Quantized High-Density Electron-Hole Plasma in Semiconductor Quantum Wells|year=2006 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.237401 |last1=Jho |first1=Y. D. |last2=Wang |first2=Xiaoming |last3=Kono |first3=J. |last4=Reitze |first4=D. H. |last5=Wei |first5=X. |last6=Belyanin |first6=A. A. |last7=Kocharovsky |first7=V. V. |last8=Kocharovsky |first8=Vl. V. |last9=Solomon |first9=G. S. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=96 |issue=23 |article-number=237401 |pmid=16803400 |arxiv=cond-mat/0601483 |bibcode=2006PhRvL..96w7401J |s2cid=14293896 }}</ref> Kocharovsky developed also a method of a phenomenological [[quantum electrodynamics]] of active media for an analysis of such collective quantum instabilities in nonequilibrium systems.<ref>{{cite book|title=Nonlinear Waves|series=Research Reports in Physics |year=1989 |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-74366-5 |bibcode=1989nowa.book.....G |isbn=978-3-540-50654-6 |last1=Gaponov-Grekhov |first1=Andrei V. |last2=Rabinovich |first2=Mikhail I. |last3=Engelbrecht |first3=Jüri }}</ref>

In 2015, Kocharovsky suggested a microscopic theory of critical phenomena in phase transitions,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Microscopic theory of phase transitions in a critical region|year=2015 |doi=10.1088/0031-8949/90/10/108002 |last1=Kocharovsky |first1=Vitaly V. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=Vladimir V. |journal=Physica Scripta |volume=90 |issue=10 |article-number=108002 |arxiv=1510.07341 |bibcode=2015PhyS...90j8002K |s2cid=73631158 }}</ref> in particular, for the Ising model of [[ferromagnetism]] and Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC). In 2020, he revealed a universality of a matrix permanent for description of major nature's complexities in critical phenomena, quantum information processes in many-body physics, fractal structures and chaos, number theory, and ♯P-hard problems in the theory of computational complexity.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Unification of the Nature's Complexities via a Matrix Permanent—Critical Phenomena, Fractals, Quantum Computing, ♯P-Complexity|year=2020 |doi=10.3390/e22030322 |doi-access=free |last1=Kocharovsky |first1=Vitaly |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=Vladimir |last3=Tarasov |first3=Sergey |journal=Entropy |volume=22 |issue=3 |page=322 |pmid=33286096 |pmc=7516781 |bibcode=2020Entrp..22..322K }}</ref> Kocharovsky developed an analytical theory of anomalous BEC fluctuations and found a universal structure of the lambda-point in the critical region of BEC for an ideal gas.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Analytical theory of mesoscopic Bose-Einstein condensation in an ideal gas|year=2010 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.81.033615 |last1=Kocharovsky |first1=Vitaly V. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=Vladimir V. |journal=Physical Review A |volume=81 |issue=3 |article-number=033615 |arxiv=1511.01610 |bibcode=2010PhRvA..81c3615K |s2cid=91173651 }}</ref> He also calculated BEC fluctuations outside the critical region for the interacting gas with a homogeneous<ref>{{cite journal|title=Condensation of N bosons. III. Analytical results for all higher moments of condensate fluctuations in interacting and ideal dilute Bose gases via the canonical ensemble quasiparticle formulation|year=2000 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.61.053606 |last1=Kocharovsky |first1=V. V. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=Vl. V. |last3=Scully |first3=Marlan O. |journal=Physical Review A |volume=61 |issue=5 |article-number=053606 |bibcode=2000PhRvA..61e3606K }}</ref> or inhomogeneous<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.102.043315|title=Bose-Einstein-condensate fluctuations versus an interparticle interaction|year=2020 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.102.043315 |last1=Tarasov |first1=S. V. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=Vl. V. |last3=Kocharovsky |first3=V. V. |journal=Physical Review A |volume=102 |issue=4 |article-number=043315 |arxiv=2007.15753 |bibcode=2020PhRvA.102d3315T |s2cid=220919815 }}</ref> condensate and discussed a challenging problem of their observation that is much deeper than a mean-field level of the many-body statistical physics. In 1988, Kocharovsky suggested a Bragg-Coulomb mechanism of a [[high-temperature superconductivity]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://jetpletters.ru/ps/1110/article_16784.shtml|title=Bragg-Coulomb double-flow mechanism for high-Tc superconductivity}}</ref>

Kocharovsky proposed a mechanism for particle acceleration through multiple conversions between charged (protons, electrons) to neutral (neutrons, photons) states which could explain the origin of cosmic rays of the ultra-high energies up to 10<sup>21</sup> eV.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Particle acceleration through multiple conversions from a charged into a neutral state and back|year=2003 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.68.043003 |last1=Derishev |first1=E. V. |last2=Aharonian |first2=F. A. |last3=Kocharovsky |first3=V. V. |last4=Kocharovsky |first4=Vl. V. |journal=Physical Review D |volume=68 |issue=4 |article-number=043003 |arxiv=astro-ph/0301263 |bibcode=2003PhRvD..68d3003D |hdl=1969.1/181988 |s2cid=119377825 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> He pointed out the inevitable presence and important role of free neutrons in the dynamics and emission of relativistic shock waves and jets in a vicinity of compact astrophysical sources, including a neutrino production in a neutron-proton relativistic wind.<ref>{{cite journal|title=The Neutron Component in Fireballs of Gamma-Ray Bursts: Dynamics and Observable Imprints|year=1999 |doi=10.1086/307574 |last1=Derishev |first1=E. V. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=V. V. |last3=Kocharovsky |first3=Vl. V. |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |volume=521 |issue=2 |pages=640–649 |bibcode=1999ApJ...521..640D |s2cid=121893123 |doi-access=free }}</ref> He found that a [[Hawking radiation]] of [[primordial black hole]]s is not observable in and above the GeV energy range due to an electromagnetic cascade in an ejected plasma.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Gamma-ray bursts from the final stage of primordial black hole evaporation|year=1996 |doi=10.1093/mnras/283.2.626 |last1=Belyanin |first1=A. A. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=V. V. |last3=Kocharovsky |first3=V. V. |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |volume=283 |issue=2 |pages=626–634 |doi-access=free }}</ref> In 1999, Kocharovsky developed a model of a compact star collapse and a subsequent gamma-ray burst induced by a primordial black hole coming inside the star.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1134/1.568241|title=Cosmological γ-ray bursts from a neutron star collapse induced by a primordial black hole|year=1999 |doi=10.1134/1.568241 |last1=Derishev |first1=E. V. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=V. V. |last3=Kocharovsky |first3=Vl. V. |journal=Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics Letters |volume=70 |issue=10 |pages=652–658 |bibcode=1999JETPL..70..652D |s2cid=122067780 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He predicted the annihilation cyclotron lines of gamma radiation from a neutron star and developed the theory of the X-ray cyclotron line formation in the atmosphere of a neutron star with due account for a spectral redistribution of photons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/pdf/2011/07/aa17240-11.pdf|title=Spectral redistribution of gyroresonant photons in magnetized atmospheres of isolated compact stars}}</ref> Kocharovsky found new classes of the current sheets and filaments with a self-consistent magnetic field in collisionless relativistic plasma<ref>{{cite journal|title=Self-Consistent Current Sheets and Filaments in Relativistic Collisionless Plasma with Arbitrary Energy Distribution of Particles|year=2010 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.215002 |last1=Kocharovsky |first1=V. V. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=Vl. V. |last3=Martyanov |first3=V. Ju. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=104 |issue=21 |article-number=215002 |pmid=20867108 |bibcode=2010PhRvL.104u5002K }}</ref> and studied the features of multiscale current structures, including turbulent ones, in both cosmic and laboratory plasmas.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Analytical theory of self-consistent current structures in a collisionless plasma|year=2016 |doi=10.3367/UFNe.2016.08.037893 |last1=Kocharovsky |first1=V. V. |last2=Kocharovsky |first2=Vl. V. |last3=Martyanov |first3=V Yu |last4=Tarasov |first4=S. V. |journal=Physics-Uspekhi |volume=59 |issue=12 |pages=1165–1210 |bibcode=2016PhyU...59.1165K |doi-access=free }}</ref>
